p: Jehoiada the priest: Who was a faithful counsellor and governed him by the word of God.
Israel money to repair the house: He does not mean the ten tribes but only the two tribes of Judah and Benjamin.
chief: For he was the high priest.
wicked woman: The scriptures call her wicked because she was a cruel murderer and a blasphemous idolater.
the chest was brought unto the: Such as were faithful men whom the king had appointed for that matter.
Jehoiada gave it to such as: Signifying that this was done by advise and counsel and not by any one man's desire.
vessels for the house of the: For the wicked kings, his predecessors and Athaliah had destroyed the vessels of the temple, or turned them to the use of their idols.
kings: Signifying that they could not honour him too much, who had so excellently served in the work of the Lord, and in the affairs of the commonwealth.
princes of Judah: Who were liars and knew now that the king was destitute of him who watched over him as a father, and therefore brought him to most vile idolatry.
testified against them: They took heaven and earth and all creatures to witness that unless they returned to the Lord, he would most grievously punish their infidelity and rebellion, Ne 9:26.
above the people: In a place above the people, to the intent that he might be heard.

commandment of the king in the: There is no rage so cruel and beastly as of them whose hearts God has hardened, and who delight more in superstition and idolatry than in the true service of God and pure simplicity of his word.

look upon it: Avenge my death and require my blood at your hands: or he speaks this by prophecy because he knew that God would do it. This Zachariah is also called the son of Barachias, Mt 23:35 because his progenitors were Iddo, Berachiah, Jehoiada.
executed judgment against Joash: That is, reproved and checked him, and handled him rigorously.
sons of Jehoiada the priest: Meaning Zachariah, who was one of Jehoiada's sons and a prophet of the Lord.
repairing of the house of God: Or, foundation.
